deities: Lord Hanuman as Dhyana Anjaneya Swamy (stone idol in meditation posture, east-facing, meditating on Lord Rama - presiding)

history.period: 12th century - built c. 1198 CE by Kakatiya king Prola II (some sources say 1143 CE under Prataparudra II - conflict, verify)
history.summary: One of Hyderabad's oldest temples, the Dhyana Anjaneya Swamy temple at Karmanghat (near Santoshnagar, off the Nagarjuna Sagar/Inner Ring Road, Saroornagar area of greater Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy district). Legend: the Kakatiya king Prola II, resting under a tree after a hunt, heard the chanting of Rama's name and found a stone idol of Hanuman seated in meditation; Hanuman appeared in his dream that night and asked for a temple, built c. 1198 CE (other accounts give 1143 under Prataparudra II - flag the conflict). The east-facing temple spreads over about 3 acres with a small koneru (pond) where devotees dip before darshan. A famous legend explains the name 'Karmanghat': Aurangzeb's army could not breach the compound wall, and the emperor himself, attempting to demolish it, heard a heavenly voice - 'Mandir todna hai rajan, to kar man ghat' ('if you would break the temple, king, first make your heart strong') - 'karo man ghat' becoming Karmanghat. Tuesdays and Saturdays draw the heaviest crowds; annadanam (free meal) is served daily; vehicle pooja is popular. Managed by Sri Karmanghat Hanuman Devasthanam (official site karmanghattemple.telangana.gov.in).
